overview: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a partial building demolition at 970 Fellsway, lot variances for a single-family home at 7 Grant Avenue, and a commercial-to-residential conversion at 612–614 Main Street. A proposal to construct a three-unit townhouse at 85 Elm Street was continued to January 30 for additional financial data and architectural renderings.

items.title: 85 Elm Street (Case A-2024-25)
items.summary: Continued to January 30, 2025, an application by 835 Elm Street LLC seeking use and dimensional variances to demolish an auto repair shop and build a three-unit townhouse, allowing the applicant to provide detailed site costs and updated renderings without screening trees.

items.title: 970 Fellsway (Case A-2024-26)
items.summary: Approved a special permit for The Davis Companies to demolish a portion of an existing nonconforming commercial structure to facilitate a lot split that preserves the remaining self-storage building's lot coverage ratio alongside an approved residential project.

items.title: 7 Grant Avenue (Case A-2024-27)
items.summary: Approved lot width and lot area variances allowing Michael and Elaine Horahan to construct a single-family dwelling on an undersized 4,500-square-foot lot created by dividing their existing residential parcel.

items.title: 612–614 Main Street (Case A-2024-28)
items.summary: Approved a special permit allowing Keith Fallon to convert an existing first-floor commercial unit into a residential unit, creating a three-unit residential structure in a general residence district.

items.title: Administrative Updates
items.summary: Staff reported that meeting minutes were delayed and noted that state regulations classify hot tubs deeper than two feet as swimming pools subject to six-foot setbacks.
